patch:
diff --git a/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py b/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
index 55fa844..732136e 100644
--- a/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
+++ b/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
@@ -1,11 +1,10 @@
-from store import CUSTOMERS, ORDERS
+from store import ORDERS
 
 
 def orders_for_customer(customer):
     """All orders belonging to `customer`."""
     rows = []
     for order in ORDERS:
-        owner = next(c for c in CUSTOMERS if c["id"] == order["customer_id"])
-        if owner["name"] == customer["name"]:
+        if order["customer_id"] == customer["id"]:
             rows.append(order)
     return rows
verification: 1) Baseline python3 run_tests.py -> 'visible tests passed' (tests too weak to catch the bug). 2) Baseline report before fix printed duplicated lines: ('a@acme.test',101,50),('a@acme.test',102,75),('b@acme.test',101,50),('b@acme.test',102,75),('z@zenith.test',103,20),('z@zenith.test',104,20) total 290 -- orders 101/102 each appear twice, each Acme sees the other's order. 3) After fix run_tests.py -> 'visible tests passed'. 4) After-fix report: 4 correct lines, total 165, orders 103 and 104 both present. 5) git diff shows only the queries.py change.
cause: orders_for_customer matched orders by comparing names instead of the unique customer id; two customers share the name 'Acme', so every Acme order was attributed to both. Fix matches by order["customer_id"] == customer["id"]; now-unused CUSTOMERS import removed.
